text:
Maya: heads-up — onboarding a community GPT variant and seeing intermittent failures in the Redwood loader. stack trace points at KV cache reshape.
Ryan: error logs?
Maya: short dump: 
```
ERROR: mismatch between num_key_value_heads (8) and model.heads (12) during kv_cache.reshape
Traceback...
```
Maya: model config.json has "num_key_value_heads": 8 but HF weights I/O claims 12. also rope_scaling present as {"type":"scale", "factor":0.8} which our converter doesn't handle.
Lisa: oh that rope_scaling shape change can shift rotary pos embeddings relative to max_position_embeddings. Did tokenizer.already include special tokens? sometimes that changes effective max length.
Sam: we saw similar with quantized 4-bit runs — sliding_window enabled in config made decode start doing off-by-one chunking and triggered N/A for some cached past keys.
Maya: examples:
- config.json: "max_position_embeddings": 2048
- tokenizer: adds BOS and multi-token special: "<chat_start>" -> becomes 2 tokens sometimes
- converter assumed unchanged token count so KV layout was wrong
Ryan: likely root cause: converter assumes num_key_value_heads == num_attention_heads / heads_per_kv (legacy) but some HF model forks expose explicit num_key_value_heads that don't map one-to-one.
Lisa: workaround I used: run a quick inspection script during onboarding that compares these fields and rewrites config to align with weights metadata. snippet I used:
```
# pseudo
hf = load_hf_config()
weights = inspect_weights_header()
if hf.get('num_key_value_heads') != compute_from(weights):
    hf['num_key_value_heads'] = compute_from(weights)
# also normalize rope_scaling to 'none' or to a simple float
```
Maya: yeah can we add this to the conversion pipeline? also special_tokens_map: {"cls":"<s>"} -> some chat templates expect <s> and others expect <s> <role>, causing template mismatch.
config-bot: automated check failed: sliding_window present -> flagged for manual review :warning:
Sam: for quantization tests, we should pin sliding_window=false and validate that chunking is handled by runtime instead. sliding_window in config often assumes HF attention kernel behavior which differs from our fused kernels.
Ryan: plan: 1) add preflight checks that compare num_key_value_heads, max_position_embeddings, rope_scaling format, and special token count. 2) if rope_scaling is an object, translate to scalar factor and log change. 3) fail fast with clear message if sliding_window=true. 4) add a small unit test per onboarding job that runs a 1k token rollforward to validate KV alignment.
Lisa: agree. I'll open a tiny PR with the preflight checks + a conversion map for common rope_scaling shapes. will include example messages to show the exact change.
Maya: thanks — also adding a regression eval that compares logits at a few seeds between HF weights and converted model (cheap, 10 seeds) to catch subtle shifts from tokenization/special token differences.
Ryan: perfect. add an alert in Console under model-onboarding if preflight mutates config so infra knows about conversions. :+1:
Maya: awesome, assigning follow-ups in the thread. will paste the PR link when ready.
